summary: The root LMM primarily means to collect, gather, or bring together. It can also refer to approaching or drawing near.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: لَمَّ ٱللّٰهُ شَعَثَهُ God rectified, or repaired, and consolidated, what was disorganized, disordered, or unsettled, of his affairs. (S.)
لَمَّمَ He made a لِمَّة of his hair. (Z, TA in art. جم.)

أَلَمَّ بِالقَوْمِ He came to the people, and alighted at their abode as a guest. (Msb.) See أَطَافَ. And hence, أَلَمَّ بِالمَعْنَى (assumed tropical:) He knew the meaning. (Msb.) And أَلَمَّ بَال َّنْبِ (assumed tropical:) He committed the sin, or offence. (Msb.) And أَلَمَّ He, or it, visited covertly; (Ham, p. 23;) or in a light, slight, or hasty manner. (Idem, pp. 385 and 815.) It became near. (Msb.) It happened. (Ham, p. 385.) أَلَمَّ بِهِ He came to him. (Ham, p. 127.) I. q.
اِلْتَمَّ It was collected, accumulated. التمّوا They collected themselves; congregated.

لَمْ with an aor. following it is often to be rendered in English by the preterperfect: ex., لَمْ أَرَهُ مُ ُ يَوْمَانِ I have not seen him for two days. لَمْ يَضْرِبْ He did not beat. (S, &c.) See also لَمَّا. أَلَمْ: see the latter half of art. أَلَا; and the former part of art. أَمَا.
لَمَمٌ A slight insanity or diabolical possession; (Mgh, Msb:) a slight taint or infection of insanity. See طَيْفٌ.
لَمَّةٌ A touch, or somewhat [ of a taint or an infection of insanity ], from the jinn. (S, K.) See لَمَمٌ.
لِمَّةٌ Hair that descends below the lobe of the ear. (S, K.) But see وَفْرَةٌ: and see a tropical use of it in a verse of Kumeyt cited in art. حف, p. 597 c.
مُلِمَّةٌ A misfortune that befalls in the present world. (S.) See an ex. in a verse cited voce حَجَا.
مُلَمَّمٌ A boy having a لِمَّة. (IDrd, TA, voce مُجَمَّمٌ.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
